correctness.rationale: The degree-81 tame diagonal cover has five inertia groups of order 3, giving genus 55. The index-three quotient projectors split the 2-divisible group: pullback and norm induce the projector to the subgroup invariants since the subgroup order is odd, and the trivial invariant summand is zero. Nontrivial character pairs have support counts 10,10,15,5 for sizes 2,3,4,5, with quotient genus support size minus two. The support-three elliptics are supersingular. For an independent support-four check, normalize the quotient to y³=(t−a)(t−b)(t−c)² with infinity the fourth branch point and put z=y²/(t−c). The regular forms dt/y and dt/z give Cartier maps to √(a+b)·dt/z and dt/y, so both directions are invertible. In support-five normalize to a monic squarefree quartic. Cartier sends dt/y to √s₃·dt/y²+√s₁·t dt/y², kills dt/y² and sends t dt/y² to dt/y. Squarefreeness rules out s₁=s₃=0, so the rank is always two; the stable rank is two for s₁≠0 and zero otherwise. Summing gives a=15 and 2-rank 40−2m. Sending the distinguished point to infinity gives s₁ as the sum of its four finite roots; clearing the nonzero denominators gives exactly the five P_i. For their intersections, write the first four loci as μ=λ+1, λ/(λ+1), 1/λ, λ², and the fifth as μ²=λ. The ten comparisons give λ²+λ+1 up to factors λ and λ+1; conversely each root with μ=λ+1 lies on all five. The gradients are nonzero on the smooth marked locus and at the intersections give slopes 0,1,α,α²,∞. This verifies the complete ordered-marked stratification without extrapolation from finite-field data.

evidence: Use Hidalgo's θ_(r;α) notation with three digit exponents α, and pair α with its negative modulo 3; the z-character is given by r+1 modulo 3. The five full-support blocks have 1-dimensional halves generated by θ_(0;111), θ_(1;111), θ_(1;211), θ_(1;121), θ_(1;112). Reading the short parity rows of the published table and applying Cartier a second time gives the respective coefficients (λ+μ+λμ)^(1/4), (1+λ+μ)^(1/4), 1+(λμ)^(1/4), μ^(1/4)+λ^(1/2), λ^(1/4)+μ^(1/2). For example θ_(0;111) maps to √(λ+μ+λμ)·θ_(1;222)+θ_(4;222), with the first target returning to θ_(0;111) and the second killed.

Each of the five blocks has rank two and contributes stable rank two exactly when that coefficient is nonzero. The smaller branch supports give ranks 0 and 30 in total by genus-one supersingularity and prior type-(3,3) rank six for each four-point subset. The table's last kernel remark is not needed: the mixed full-support blocks can have a one-dimensional kernel generated by a linear combination of two basis elements.

The equations from the five zero coefficients, in the smooth locus, reduce to four fractional functions of λ and μ²=λ. Comparing them and removing excluded denominators gives λ²+λ+1 in each pair, and their slopes at those roots follow by differentiation.

originality.rationale: The headline invariants are covered by mechanical specialization and iteration of Hidalgo's published Cartier table on precisely the same marked family and by his lower-type calculation. Though the assembled stratification is not stated in the inspected text, the five controlling coefficients are explicit in its small Cartier blocks (extraction below), not just computable in principle from a general method. The additional marked intersections and tangents follow by elementary comparison and differentiation of those loci. This is an implied specialization, not an allegation that the same prose already appeared or that the frozen theorem is false.

value.rationale: Knowing the exact 2-rank loci of a natural generalized Fermat family is useful, and the cyclic quotient proof is clear. But the claimed invariant classification is the direct low-dimensional-block extraction described above from the published table for the same family, plus the ordinary support-four input. The remaining smooth marked intersection and tangent description follows by routine algebra on those exact equations. No independent strengthening (for example a torsion or Newton polygon statement) is claimed that would make this a separate scientific finding.
